feature.summary: Neither a way to opt into experimental or preview features nor a reset-all-preferences action exists on any app. The only restore action is 'Restore defaults' in the Keyboard pane on web and Desktop, which resets shortcut switches and recorded keys only. The brief marks restore defaults as not applicable, which the code contradicts.

purpose.what_it_does: Would let a person join preview features and put all preferences back to defaults. Today only the shortcut reset exists.
purpose.why_it_exists: Leading assistants let people try early features and reset settings after experiments. The brief's S84.25 and S84.26 record both as expected.
purpose.who_uses_it: Early adopters wanting previews; anyone whose settings are in a confusing state.
problems_solved: No way to return to a known state
No opt-in path for preview features
use_cases: A person undoes all shortcut changes with one press.
A future opt-in toggle for a preview feature [proposed].
A future reset of appearance and composer choices [proposed].

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: Settings, General, 'Keyboard shortcuts', 'View shortcuts', then 'Restore defaults' at the bottom of the Keyboard pane (apps/web/features/chat/components/dialogs/KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx:330-340).
Experimental enrolment: not found on web, Desktop, mobile, VS Code or Chrome (searched settings code for 'experimental', 'early access', 'preview features').
screens_and_controls: Button 'Restore defaults' (disabled while nothing is changed) and a live summary of how many shortcuts are off or changed.

Confirmation 'Restore default shortcuts?' with text 'Every key combination you recorded goes back to its default and every shortcut turns back on. To use your own keys again you would record them again.' and button 'Restore defaults' (KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx:230-245).
journey: Confirm if keys were recorded; if only switches were off, it resets without asking.
feedback_and_outputs: Summary text clears; keys show defaults; the button becomes disabled.
settings: disabledShortcutIds and shortcutBindings are the only values reset.

working: restoreShortcutDefaults sets disabledShortcutIds and shortcutBindings to empty (apps/web/shared/stores/web-settings-store.ts:96, 158).
The button is disabled when nothing differs from defaults, and asks before discarding recorded keys (KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx:206-245, 337).
incomplete: The reset covers shortcuts only; it does not touch theme, text size, send key, sidebar items or notifications.
not_available: Experimental or preview enrolment on all apps.
Any reset on CLI, VS Code, Chrome (they use host or config file editing).

established.statement: The user can opt into experimental or preview features from settings.
established.source: S84.25 (area brief); missing on every app

established.statement: Settings offer a restore-defaults action that resets preferences.
established.source: S84.26 (area brief); the brief says not applicable anywhere, but the code has a shortcut-only reset

established.statement: An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence; useConfirmAction is the surface.

acceptance_criteria: Restore defaults is disabled when shortcuts are at defaults.
After switching a shortcut off, Restore defaults is enabled and one press turns it back on without a dialog.
After recording keys, Restore defaults asks 'Restore default shortcuts?' before acting.
After confirming, recorded keys and switches are cleared and the summary text is empty.
Other preferences (send switch, theme, sidebar items) are unchanged by this button.
inferred: A general reset would need to clear account-synced fields too, or the next sync would restore them [inferred from CloudSettingsSync hydration].
proposed: [proposed] Decide whether experimental opt-in is wanted; if so, add a section backed by feature flags and the account.
[proposed] Add a 'Reset settings' action in General with a confirmation listing what changes, covering the appearance namespace and device stores.
[proposed] Correct S84.26 from 'not applicable' to 'partial: shortcuts only'.

corrections.claim: The store persists the empty values to localStorage (web-settings-store.ts:216-219)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The file is only 214 lines, so 216-219 does not exist. Persistence is the zustand persist config at lines 209-212 (name 'agiworkforce-web-settings', createJSONStorage(localStorage)). It persists the whole store, with no partialize.
corrections.correction: The store persists the whole state, including the emptied shortcut values, to localStorage via persist (web-settings-store.ts:209-212).

corrections.claim: Restore defaults lives on Desktop too, via the same Settings, General, Keyboard pane (WebSettingsModal.tsx:297)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: WebSettingsModal.tsx:297 mounts KeyboardShortcutsPane for web (the Electron desktop shows hosted web, so this holds). However, the Tauri desktop source has its own separate reset, resetAllCustomKeybindings, wired in KeybindingsSettings.tsx:256 with a confirm, and the page does not mention it.
corrections.correction: Add that the retained Tauri desktop code has its own keybinding reset (resetAllCustomKeybindings), separate from the web store.

missing_facts: The retained Tauri desktop app has its own confirmed reset of custom keybindings (resetAllCustomKeybindings), separate from the web store: apps/desktop/src/features/settings/KeybindingsSettings.tsx:256-264, apps/desktop/src/stores/settingsStore.ts:201.

The web store persist config has no partialize, so the whole store (including customCommands) lives in one localStorage key and the shortcut reset does not clear it: apps/web/shared/stores/web-settings-store.ts:209-212.
The confirmation is created with destructive:false, so it is shown as non-destructive although recorded chords are discarded: KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx:~238.
